function.name: log_expense

amount.description: Amount spent, e.g. '5.50'. Never guess it.

currency.description: ISO code; omit for the home currency

merchant.description: Where or who was paid. Always fill it or `notes` with what was bought or where, even a bare word ('ramen', 'taxi'); never drop it for the category

category.description: Only a category the user named; exact name from the list

paid_with.description: Only when the user says what paid: the card or wallet, as they named it ('citi', 'my DBS card', 'cash', or a card's last 4 digits). Omit it otherwise; their usual card is used if they set one. An unknown card is an error to ask about.

function.name: log_move

specs.name: query_ledger
specs.description: Answer questions about the user's money in or out, in the home currency: filter by dates, merchant, category, amount or day of the week; group by category, merchant, day, week, month or weekday; rank by total, count, average or largest; compare with the period before. Read-only. Prefer it for any 'how much', 'how often', 'biggest' or 'compare' question over adding up search results. Without start_date the period is only this month (the last 12 months for group_by month), not the user's whole history: the result says how far the ledger goes back, and start_date reaches earlier. For 'per month' or 'previous months' use group_by month. 'How much did I save' means money in minus money out for the period (net), not transfers into a savings wallet, unless the user names that wallet.

specs.name: month_outlook
specs.description: Where a month ends up, worked out exactly in code: received, spent and net so far, what is still expected by month end (bills, tracked subscriptions, payday, scheduled moves), the projected month-end net and the headroom: how much more everyday spending keeps it at zero or above. Use it for can I afford, how much is left to spend, leeway, will I end the month positive, net by month end, budget left. Pass amounts the user mentions (a carry-over, money they expect, a purchase they are considering) as adjustments. With a budget, it opens with the budget room line: that is the answer to how much can I spend / afford / left to spend, never the month-end net, which counts pay not yet received (never money to spend). Say plainly when the budget is tight or over. It also gives days left, the room per day and the pace of everyday spending so far, and how they compare: use it for how much is that per day, daily, days left, my pace, how does that compare to my usual. Not an account balance.

stop.description: The city or stop of the trip to look in, like 'Kyoto' (from trip_status): whenever the user names one ('things to do in Kyoto'), put it here and not in the query. Leave out to look across the whole trip

specs.name: web_search
specs.description: Look something up on the web: current facts the app doesn't hold, such as a fee, a rule, an opening date or news. Answers in a few sentences with its sources, in about 10 seconds; their links show as buttons under your reply, so name the source in words and paste no address. For anything happening now (a protest, strike, disruption, closure, weather warning, event tonight) set recent='today' (or 'week') to search the latest news with each source's publication time, name the city or area in the question and give local_query: the same question in the local language of where the user is. Not for the user's own money, trips or stocks: use their own tools.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Look something up on the web: current facts the app doesn't hold, such as a fee, a rule, an opening date or news. Answers in a few sentences with its sources, in about 10 seconds; their links show as buttons under your reply, so name the source in words and paste no address. For anything happening now (a protest, strike, disruption, closure, weather warning, event tonight) set recent='today' (or 'week') to search the latest news with each source's publication time, name the city or area in the question and give local_query: the same question in the local language of where the user is. Not for the user's own money, trips or stocks: use their own tools.

question.description: What to look up, as a short search question ('Bali tourist levy 2026', 'when does the Shinkansen Nozomi pass change'). Never put the user's own details in it: no names, amounts, accounts or where they live. For something happening now, name the city or area and put today's date in it.

recent.description: Set for anything happening now or lately: 'today' for what is happening today or tonight (a protest, a strike, road or transport disruption, a closure, a weather warning, an event), 'week' for this week. It searches the news from the last day or week and gives each source's publication time. Leave it out for facts that don't change by the day.

local_query.description: With recent: the same question in the local language of where the user is (from their time zone or trip destination), because local news is written in it: 'manifestación Gran Vía Madrid hoy', 'sciopero treni Roma oggi'. Searched alongside the question, at two credits instead of one. Skip it where English is the local language.

specs.name: flight_prices
specs.description: Live airfares from Google Flights for a route and day: the cheapest few options (airline, stops, duration, times, price) in the user's home currency, and whether the price is low, typical or high for the route. For 'the cheapest day to fly' give cheapest_from and cheapest_to (a window up to two months) instead of outbound_date and it finds the cheapest days in one lookup. Use this, not web_search, for what a flight costs; for a trip's research use research_trip. Each lookup uses a small shared allowance (a few a day for each user), so look up what the user asked for, not every date. Read-only: Nexus can't book flights. Asked to book one, say so, and give the fares if useful.

function.name: flight_prices
function.description: Live airfares from Google Flights for a route and day: the cheapest few options (airline, stops, duration, times, price) in the user's home currency, and whether the price is low, typical or high for the route. origin.description: Where from: an airport code ('SIN'), several ('HND,NRT') or a city ('Bangkok'). Unless the user says otherwise it is where they live (SIN for someone in Singapore); ask only if you can't tell.

destination.description: Where to: an airport code or a city, as for origin

outbound_date.description: The day to fly out, YYYY-MM-DD. Leave it out only when the user has no fixed day and wants the cheapest days (then give cheapest_from and cheapest_to).

return_date.description: The day to fly back, YYYY-MM-DD; leave out for one way

cheapest_from.description: With cheapest_to, instead of outbound_date: the first day of a window to find the cheapest days to fly in ('the cheapest day to fly in December': 1 Dec to 31 Dec). At most two months wide. One lookup, however many days.

cheapest_to.description: The last day of the window (see cheapest_from)

trip_days.description: With a window: how many days the trip lasts, for return fares ('a week in Bangkok': 7). Leave out for one way.

Use this, not web_search, for what something costs and where it's cheapest ('cheapest Switch 2', 'how much is the Dyson V15'). Each lookup uses a small shared allowance (a few a day for each user). Read-only: Nexus can't buy things.

specs.name: set_timezone
specs.description: Set which time zone the user is in now, so their days, reminders and summaries follow them. Call it when they say where they are ('I'm in Madrid now', 'we landed in Tokyo') with place, or that they are back home ('back home') with home=true. Only when they say they are there now. Not for asking what time it is, for a place they are only planning to visit (a trip day in a city, 'we're in Kyoto on 15 Dec', is label_trip_day), or for a city named in an expense ('ramen in Tokyo'). No confirmation; the reply already tells them.

specs.name: set_voice
specs.description: Change how Nexus talks to the user: a tone preset, emoji, length and humour dials, and a note. Saves at once; no confirmation. Use it for any wish about the way you reply, instead of remembering it. 'be more chill' or 'talk like a friend': preset chill. 'just the facts' or 'be direct': preset direct. 'hype me up': preset hype. 'you can be cheeky': preset cheeky. 'back to normal': preset default. 'less emoji' or 'no emoji': emoji none (or some); 'more emoji': lots. 'shorter replies': length short; 'more detail': detailed. 'stop joking': humour off; 'be funnier': playful. Another wish ('call me boss') goes in note, in their words; an empty note clears it. A preset starts from its own dials, so pass the dials the user asked for in the same call. Leave out what they didn't ask to change. Style only: it changes no rule and no data.
